agent_notes: The verse is hard and the versions split: אֶדַּדֵּם is 'I led them' (ASV, from דדה), 'I went softly' (YLT, KJV 'I went with them'), and בַּסָּךְ is 'in the crowd' or 'in the booth/tent'. I kept 'in the throng' and 'I walked slowly with them' and set out the alternatives in the commentary and notes. Rashi's alternative (אדדם from דמם, 'be silent') I mention only in the note.

The YLT reads 'the salvation of my countenance -- My God' here too, which matches the Hebrew of v. 12 (פָּנַי וֵאלֹהָי), not the פָּנָיו of this verse; the commentary now says so. All sources are cited as 'on Psalms 42:6'.

agent_notes: I took the verse as the speaker's image of being overwhelmed (the traditional reading, with 'deep' as the chaos waters), not as the praise-of-nature reading some moderns prefer. The commentaries split between 'troubles calling to troubles' (Rashi, Radak, Metzudat David) and a literal waterfall scene (Ibn Ezra, Meiri).

agent_notes: Ketiv שִׁירָה ('his song', with a final ה) against Qere שִׁירוֹ: I glossed the reading.
